{
  "project_id": "P-PAK-ResilientAccessibleMicrofinance",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Flood‑induced surge in non‑performing loans erodes capital adequacy of microfinance banks, threatening liquidity.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Activate CRF contingent liquidity immediately; maintain capital buffers; use parametric insurance; monitor NPL trends closely.",
      "evidence": "NPLs of MFBs surged by 25.7% after the 2022 floods, eroding capital adequacy (section 9)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "CRF may lack sufficient capital if multiple extreme flood events occur during the project period.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Conduct annual stress tests; secure additional donor or private capital; retain insurance backstop; set aside reserve funds.",
      "evidence": "CRF capitalized to meet contingent financing needs; expansion requires additional capital (sections 21‑30)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Delay in activating CRF triggers due to slow data provision from third‑party providers.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Pre‑establish data‑sharing agreements with providers; define strict timelines; use real‑time monitoring; have backup data sources.",
      "evidence": "Data required to evaluate triggers will be provided by third‑party service providers (section 31)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Governance risk: SBP as trustee may face conflicts of interest or capacity constraints.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Define clear fiduciary duties; create independent oversight committee; enforce regular external audits; adopt conflict‑of‑interest policies.",
      "evidence": "SBP will be the executing agency and trustee, selected after extensive due diligence (section 38)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Legal risk: Amendments to the Trust Deed require Association consent, potentially delaying actions.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Obtain pre‑approval for likely amendments; maintain open communication with the Association; include emergency amendment clause.",
      "evidence": "Trust Deed cannot be amended without prior written consent of the Association (Legal Covenants)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Insufficient qualified agritech firms may limit the Innovative Agricultural Liquidity product’s effectiveness.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Run transparent competitive AFIC selection; keep a backup list of ATCs; provide capacity‑building support to selected firms.",
      "evidence": "AFIC will identify five to six ATCs to partner with MFPs (section 26)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "MFPs may not meet eligibility criteria for CRF liquidity, reducing uptake.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Offer flexible eligibility thresholds; assist MFPs in documenting flood exposure; monitor uptake and adjust criteria as needed.",
      "evidence": "Only MFPs with active portfolios in qualifying flood‑impacted areas will be eligible (section 28)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Gender target (≥55% women beneficiaries) may not be achieved, limiting social impact.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set gender quotas; track disbursements gender‑disaggregated; enforce higher borrowing cost penalty for non‑compliance; conduct gender‑focused outreach.",
      "evidence": "Ensure at least 55% of beneficiaries are women; higher borrowing cost if deviation (section 49)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Annual decision not to purchase parametric insurance backstop could reduce CRF’s capacity during extreme events.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Allocate a dedicated budget line; perform yearly financial review; negotiate multi‑year insurance contracts to lock coverage.",
      "evidence": "Decision to secure parametric insurance for the CRF will be undertaken annually by the Oversight Committee (section 30)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Macroeconomic instability may impair MFPs’ ability to repay and maintain capital adequacy.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Monitor macro indicators; adjust liquidity provisions accordingly; coordinate with Ministry of Finance for fiscal support; diversify funding sources.",
      "evidence": "Impact of shocks exacerbated by macroeconomic crisis since 2019; sector growth receded to 2.4% in 2023 (sections 8‑9)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Delays in establishing pooled and child accounts could postpone CRF capitalization.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Prepare account‑setup plan before project start; assign dedicated treasury team; obtain bank approvals early.",
      "evidence": "Recipient will establish a pooled account with segregated child accounts; funds front‑loaded for CRF capitalization (section 43)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Inaccurate flood modelling data may trigger inappropriate CRF disbursements.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Use multiple modelling sources; validate models annually; incorporate ground‑truth data; set conservative trigger thresholds.",
      "evidence": "Risk modelling will be the basis for CRF operations and trigger thresholds (section 37)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Increased agricultural lending could lead to higher fertilizer and pesticide use, causing localized environmental degradation.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Include environmental safeguards in loan terms; promote climate‑smart agronomy; monitor soil and water quality; enforce negative list.",
      "evidence": "Cumulative impacts may increase use of fertilizers, pesticides, affecting air and water quality (section 54)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Grievance Redress Service may be ineffective, leading to stakeholder dissatisfaction and reputational risk.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish clear GRS procedures; train staff; publicize channels; monitor complaint resolution times and satisfaction.",
      "evidence": "Establishment of a functional grievance redress mechanism to be integrated fully (section 50)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Currency fluctuations between PKR and USD could erode the real value of the CRF capital.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Hedge currency exposure; maintain a reserve buffer; conduct periodic re‑valuation of capital in PKR terms.",
      "evidence": "Exchange Rate Effective Jan 31 2025: PKR 278.64 = US$1 (datasheet)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Insufficient private sector participation may limit additional funding needed for CRF sustainability.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop attractive terms for private investors; showcase pilot successes; engage private sector early through outreach events.",
      "evidence": "CRF will crowd in additional funds from government, donors, etc., to mitigate climate risks (section 39)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Expanding CRF coverage to drought or heat may be constrained by lack of data and financing.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Create phased risk‑modelling roadmap; secure contingent financing in advance; pilot additional risk products before full rollout.",
      "evidence": "Enhancing scope to other climate risks requires additional capital and adequate risk modelling (sections 30‑31)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Political changes could reduce GoP commitment to the CRF and related policy alignment.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Obtain multi‑year legislative endorsement; embed CRF in national policy frameworks; maintain broad stakeholder coalition.",
      "evidence": "Project aligns with GoP development priorities; implementation subject to GoP approval (section 3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R19",
      "description": "Compliance with ESS 9 (Financial Intermediaries) may cause procedural delays.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Conduct early compliance review; align project design with ESS 9 requirements; obtain necessary approvals promptly.",
      "evidence": "ESS 9: Financial Intermediaries Relevant (datasheet)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R20",
      "description": "Gaps in monitoring and evaluation data could hinder tracking of PDO indicators.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen MIS; set data‑quality standards; train staff on data collection; conduct independent verification audits.",
      "evidence": "M&E will use bi‑annual reviews, financial audit, MIS, beneficiary surveys (section 41)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Flood‑induced surge in non‑performing loans erodes capital adequacy of microfinance banks, threatening liquidity.
risks.mitigation: Activate CRF contingent liquidity immediately; maintain capital buffers; use parametric insurance; monitor NPL trends closely.
risks.evidence: NPLs of MFBs surged by 25.7% after the 2022 floods, eroding capital adequacy (section 9).

risks.description: CRF may lack sufficient capital if multiple extreme flood events occur during the project period.
risks.mitigation: Conduct annual stress tests; secure additional donor or private capital; retain insurance backstop; set aside reserve funds.
risks.evidence: CRF capitalized to meet contingent financing needs; expansion requires additional capital (sections 21‑30).

risks.description: Delay in activating CRF triggers due to slow data provision from third‑party providers.
risks.mitigation: Pre‑establish data‑sharing agreements with providers; define strict timelines; use real‑time monitoring; have backup data sources.
risks.evidence: Data required to evaluate triggers will be provided by third‑party service providers (section 31).

risks.description: Governance risk: SBP as trustee may face conflicts of interest or capacity constraints.
risks.mitigation: Define clear fiduciary duties; create independent oversight committee; enforce regular external audits; adopt conflict‑of‑interest policies.
risks.evidence: SBP will be the executing agency and trustee, selected after extensive due diligence (section 38).

risks.description: Legal risk: Amendments to the Trust Deed require Association consent, potentially delaying actions.
risks.mitigation: Obtain pre‑approval for likely amendments; maintain open communication with the Association; include emergency amendment clause.
risks.evidence: Trust Deed cannot be amended without prior written consent of the Association (Legal Covenants).

risks.description: Insufficient qualified agritech firms may limit the Innovative Agricultural Liquidity product’s effectiveness.
risks.mitigation: Run transparent competitive AFIC selection; keep a backup list of ATCs; provide capacity‑building support to selected firms.
risks.evidence: AFIC will identify five to six ATCs to partner with MFPs (section 26).

risks.description: MFPs may not meet eligibility criteria for CRF liquidity, reducing uptake.
risks.mitigation: Offer flexible eligibility thresholds; assist MFPs in documenting flood exposure; monitor uptake and adjust criteria as needed.
risks.evidence: Only MFPs with active portfolios in qualifying flood‑impacted areas will be eligible (section 28).

risks.description: Gender target (≥55% women beneficiaries) may not be achieved, limiting social impact.
risks.mitigation: Set gender quotas; track disbursements gender‑disaggregated; enforce higher borrowing cost penalty for non‑compliance; conduct gender‑focused outreach.
risks.evidence: Ensure at least 55% of beneficiaries are women; higher borrowing cost if deviation (section 49).

risks.description: Annual decision not to purchase parametric insurance backstop could reduce CRF’s capacity during extreme events.
risks.mitigation: Allocate a dedicated budget line; perform yearly financial review; negotiate multi‑year insurance contracts to lock coverage.
risks.evidence: Decision to secure parametric insurance for the CRF will be undertaken annually by the Oversight Committee (section 30).

risks.description: Macroeconomic instability may impair MFPs’ ability to repay and maintain capital adequacy.
risks.mitigation: Monitor macro indicators; adjust liquidity provisions accordingly; coordinate with Ministry of Finance for fiscal support; diversify funding sources.
risks.evidence: Impact of shocks exacerbated by macroeconomic crisis since 2019; sector growth receded to 2.4% in 2023 (sections 8‑9).

risks.description: Delays in establishing pooled and child accounts could postpone CRF capitalization.
risks.mitigation: Prepare account‑setup plan before project start; assign dedicated treasury team; obtain bank approvals early.
risks.evidence: Recipient will establish a pooled account with segregated child accounts; funds front‑loaded for CRF capitalization (section 43).

risks.description: Inaccurate flood modelling data may trigger inappropriate CRF disbursements.
risks.mitigation: Use multiple modelling sources; validate models annually; incorporate ground‑truth data; set conservative trigger thresholds.
risks.evidence: Risk modelling will be the basis for CRF operations and trigger thresholds (section 37).

risks.description: Increased agricultural lending could lead to higher fertilizer and pesticide use, causing localized environmental degradation.
risks.mitigation: Include environmental safeguards in loan terms; promote climate‑smart agronomy; monitor soil and water quality; enforce negative list.
risks.evidence: Cumulative impacts may increase use of fertilizers, pesticides, affecting air and water quality (section 54).

risks.description: Grievance Redress Service may be ineffective, leading to stakeholder dissatisfaction and reputational risk.
risks.mitigation: Establish clear GRS procedures; train staff; publicize channels; monitor complaint resolution times and satisfaction.
risks.evidence: Establishment of a functional grievance redress mechanism to be integrated fully (section 50).

risks.description: Currency fluctuations between PKR and USD could erode the real value of the CRF capital.
risks.mitigation: Hedge currency exposure; maintain a reserve buffer; conduct periodic re‑valuation of capital in PKR terms.
risks.evidence: Exchange Rate Effective Jan 31 2025: PKR 278.64 = US$1 (datasheet).

risks.description: Insufficient private sector participation may limit additional funding needed for CRF sustainability.
risks.mitigation: Develop attractive terms for private investors; showcase pilot successes; engage private sector early through outreach events.
risks.evidence: CRF will crowd in additional funds from government, donors, etc., to mitigate climate risks (section 39).

risks.description: Expanding CRF coverage to drought or heat may be constrained by lack of data and financing.
risks.mitigation: Create phased risk‑modelling roadmap; secure contingent financing in advance; pilot additional risk products before full rollout.
risks.evidence: Enhancing scope to other climate risks requires additional capital and adequate risk modelling (sections 30‑31).

risks.description: Political changes could reduce GoP commitment to the CRF and related policy alignment.
risks.mitigation: Obtain multi‑year legislative endorsement; embed CRF in national policy frameworks; maintain broad stakeholder coalition.
risks.evidence: Project aligns with GoP development priorities; implementation subject to GoP approval (section 3).

risks.description: Compliance with ESS 9 (Financial Intermediaries) may cause procedural delays.
risks.mitigation: Conduct early compliance review; align project design with ESS 9 requirements; obtain necessary approvals promptly.
risks.evidence: ESS 9: Financial Intermediaries Relevant (datasheet).

risks.description: Gaps in monitoring and evaluation data could hinder tracking of PDO indicators.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen MIS; set data‑quality standards; train staff on data collection; conduct independent verification audits.
risks.evidence: M&E will use bi‑annual reviews, financial audit, MIS, beneficiary surveys (section 41).
